findings.location: Prepared Scan Manifest fields at lines 19-20; CodeGraph and Java readiness value objects at lines 72 and 76; canonical-envelope.md lines 104 and 117; prepared-scan-contracts.md lines 39-41; plan.md line 140
findings.affected_requirement: Prior finding PR-003; FR-035; FR-040; SC-001; SC-003; SC-008
findings.evidence: The regenerated envelope makes CodeGraphProofHash and JavaReadinessHash direct ManifestFingerprint inputs, and exact replay includes both hard-readiness proof hashes. However, the only described preimages are bounded canonical JSON objects whose canonical JSON grammar, exact field order, null/default representation, enum representation, and field exclusions are not defined by canonical-envelope.md. More importantly, both typed proof models explicitly include measured duration, while plan.md says canonical equality includes every proof value and prepared-scan-contracts.md excludes timestamps but not durations. Fresh execution of identical readiness work naturally produces different durations, so two otherwise identical preparations can produce different proof hashes and ManifestFingerprints, contradicting the promise that completion/process timing cannot affect the result and preventing mutation-free exact replay after recomputation. The independent relational reconstructor also cannot derive these hashes from a normative byte contract.
findings.correction_outcome: Define versioned canonical envelope domains and exact field tables for CodeGraph completeness proof and Java readiness identity, and make the manifest reference those deterministic identity hashes. Separate observational duration and other volatile telemetry from replay identity while retaining it as bounded audit metadata. Specify exact stable included predicates/bindings, ordering, null/default handling, and derived exclusions. Add literal proof-envelope vectors, an independent relational reconstruction test, a repeated-preparation test where durations differ but manifest bytes remain identical, and mutation tests where any stable readiness predicate changes and replay conflicts. Regenerate downstream plan artifacts consistently.

summary: REVISE. PR-001 is closed by FR-031, AD-3, the prepared-store failure table, and golden case 5: every index/rebuild/status/runtime/identity/path/completeness/readiness failure rejects approval, while only post-readiness related-file expansion may Warning/fallback. PR-002 is closed by FR-034/FR-035, the Ordinal Participation Matrix, AD-5/AD-6, the data model, API projection, uniqueness constraints, replay rules, and interleaving vectors: ManifestOrdinal is contiguous per Repository and PairSelectionOrdinal is contiguous pair-wide. PR-004 is closed by FR-029-FR-032, AD-6, and golden cases 1-5: high-value means direct score at least 400, only the first at most 20 per Repository are mandatory seeds/expansion roots, pair comparison uses lowercase UUID D text under ordinal comparison, and retain/fill/cap behavior is exact. PR-003 closes the original ID/fingerprint cycle, tagged scalar/list/object grammar, field ordering, UUIDv8 construction, and manifest/pair dependency direction, but it is not fully closed because the two hard-readiness proof hashes entering the manifest still lack normative deterministic preimages and currently include variable durations. That High replay defect prevents ACCEPT. The remaining plan preserves the Windows-host Vulgata/CodeGraph/Java 21/JDT-LS topology, PostgreSQL-only Docker requirement, exact CodeGraph and JDT-LS versions, no CodeGraphContext, all 43 FRs and nine SCs, Constitution/project boundaries, safe XML constraints, atomic pair intent, planned-change disclosures, and Story 12.3 exclusion. Read-only checks used Get-Content -Raw over the definition set and authorities, rg -n over Story 12.2/12.3, PRD/design/runtime/proof/replay clauses and current seams, Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 over the 15 owned paths, git rev-parse HEAD, and git status --short. No file, verdict, state, index, branch, or Git history was changed.
